title: Car Bomb Explodes Outside Police Headquarters in Ojocaliente, Zacatecas — 11 Injured
detail: On August 30, 2026 (Sunday) around 7:30 PM local time, an unidentified man parked a vehicle laden with explosives in front of the municipal police (DSPM) command in Ojocaliente, Zacatecas, then fled on foot; the device detonated when an officer approached to inspect it. Eleven people were injured, including civilians and municipal police, at least two seriously. The blast damaged roughly five city blocks — at least seven homes, businesses, private vehicles and patrol units, with windows shattered throughout the area. State Security Secretary Arturo Medina Mayoral said authorities were investigating possible involvement of a Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) cell; the vehicle used had been reported stolen in Jalisco since April, and the explosive materials resembled those used in mining operations. A near-simultaneous explosion in Villa García led to the detention of an 18-year-old who claimed CJNG membership. State officials said the attack was the 17th documented explosive-device attack on security forces in Zacatecas over the prior two years and the 10th of 2026 alone, part of an escalating wave that has included motorcycle-borne devices and improvised metal-pipe bombs ("niples"). State and federal forces reinforced the area following the blast.

title: Alcalde Presents Anticorruption Package Modifying 19 Laws, Creating 2 New Ones
detail: On August 30, 2026 (Sunday), Presidential Legal Counsel Luisa María Alcalde presented Sheinbaum's anticorruption reform package to Morena's Senate caucus, ahead of formal introduction to Congress. The package modifies 19 existing laws and creates two new ones, introducing real-time technological monitoring of public spending, tighter oversight of government contracting, and mandatory "proactive transparency" in public tenders — publishing bidding information without waiting for citizen requests. The design, led by Anticorruption and Good Government Secretary Raquel Buenrostro with input from the Federal Administrative Justice Tribunal and the Federal Auditor's Office (ASF), also aims to strengthen those two institutions' capacity to pursue corruption and good-governance cases. Separately, Morena's Senate bloc proposed federal deputy Higinio Martínez to preside over the Senate's Mesa Directiva for the third year of the LXVI Legislature.
